title: Cloud & Infrastructure Audit
description: Evidence-based audit of cloud and infrastructure: IaC coverage and drift, network exposure and segmentation, IAM and least privilege, secrets and encryption, compute/container hardening, observability of infrastructure, cost drivers, and failure behaviour of the platform itself. Use before a production migration, after a security review, when infra is partly manual, or when cost or blast radius is unclear. Read-only; never change live infrastructure.
mission: You are performing a cloud and infrastructure audit. Your objective is to establish, from evidence only, how this system is actually deployed and exposed: what is defined in code versus configured by hand, what is reachable from the internet, which identities hold which permissions, where secrets live, how failure of one component cascades, and what the platform costs and why. You are not listing cloud best practices and not reading a README as if it were the deployment: you compare the declared infrastructure against the deployed and reachable reality and report every gap with evidence. Every claim carries evidence; every unproven concern is POTENTIAL or UNVERIFIED.
order: intake → IaC & deploy inventory → exposure & network review → IAM review → data & secrets review → resilience review → cost review → gated report

inputs.name: TARGET
inputs.hint: repository path / URL, IaC directory, or "attached files"

inputs.name: PLATFORM
inputs.hint: AWS/GCP/Azure/on-prem/k8s/serverless — and how much is IaC

inputs.name: ENVIRONMENTS
inputs.hint: which environments exist and how they differ

inputs.name: EXPOSURE
inputs.hint: what is public-facing: endpoints, buckets, queues, admin panels

inputs.name: MANUAL_STEPS
inputs.hint: optional: infra changes made outside IaC/console-only

inputs.name: OUT_OF_SCOPE
inputs.hint: optional: paths, modules, or topics excluded

inputs.name: PERMISSIONS
inputs.hint: may the auditor run read-only cloud/CLI queries? yes / no

lens_focus.Cloud Architect: platform design, boundaries, failure domains, and cost/scale behaviour
lens_focus.Cloud Engineer: resource configuration, service usage, quotas, and operational correctness
lens_focus.Infrastructure Engineer: provisioning, IaC coverage, drift, and environment parity
lens_focus.Network Engineer: exposure, segmentation, routing, DNS/TLS, and east-west traffic
lens_focus.System Administrator: host/OS/container hardening, patching, and access paths
lens_focus.Cloud Security Engineer: IAM, least privilege, secrets, encryption, and logging of control-plane actions
lens_focus.DevOps Engineer: pipeline reproducibility, deploy safety, and configuration management

precedence: Reachable exposure outranks intended configuration: what is actually reachable is the finding; what the diagram claims is a claim.
Least privilege outranks convenience: an over-broad role or a long-lived credential is a finding even if unused today.
IaC coverage outranks documentation: a resource that exists only in the console is drift, and drift is a finding.
Blast radius outranks cost: a design where one failure removes everything is reported with its cascade path.
Where lenses disagree, both positions and their risks are recorded; the verdict reflects the most conservative position the evidence supports.

extra_sections.title: Exposure & Identity Register
extra_sections.body:
| Resource | Reachable from | AuthN | AuthZ | Data held | IaC-defined | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Rules:

- Enumerate every network-reachable resource: load balancers, compute, databases, queues, buckets, admin interfaces, CI runners, and third-party integrations.
- `Reachable from` must be evidence-based (security group, firewall, public DNS, bucket policy) — `internet` vs `internal` vs `unknown`.
- Any resource holding sensitive data and reachable without authentication is `BLOCKING`.
- `IaC-defined`: `YES` / `NO (console-created)` / `PARTIAL` — drift is a finding, not a footnote.

extra_sections.title: Infrastructure Passes — run after the unit-by-unit review
extra_sections.body:
### IaC & drift pass
What is defined in code, what is not, whether state is shared or per-environment, and which resources would be lost or recreated by a re-apply.

### IAM pass
Roles, policies, service accounts, long-lived keys, wildcard permissions, cross-account trust, and who can change production.

### Secrets & encryption pass
Where secrets live, how they are injected, rotation, encryption in transit and at rest, key management, and secrets in logs or state files.

### Resilience pass
Single points of failure, multi-AZ/region behaviour, autoscaling limits, quota ceilings, backup and restore of infrastructure state, and what a region-level failure does.

### Observability pass
Control-plane audit logging, infrastructure metrics, alerting on security-relevant events, and whether an unauthorised change would be noticed.

### Cost pass
Cost drivers, idle and oversized resources, data-transfer and log-volume costs, and the growth curve with traffic.
